newsitem.title: USA: Iowa Legislature approves $4.3 bln FY 98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Iowa Legislature approves $4.3 bln FY 98 budget.

text.p: Iowa legislators approved a $4.3 billion general fund budget for fiscal 1998 and adjourned their session three days early, an administrative assistant to the state house speaker said Wednesday.

Legislators decided to end the session Tuesday after reaching an impasse over proposals to revise legislation governing large livestock farms and to provide partial funding for a new packing plant facility in central Iowa, said John Davis, administrative assistant to House Speaker Ron Corbett, R-Cedar Rapids.
The budget includes a 10 percent income tax cut across the board totalling $200 million and eliminates the inheritance tax for family members, providing a $46 million reduction, Davis said.
Legislators also approved $22 million of fully funded tax credits to local governments for the next fiscal year, Davis noted.
The budget also includes $111 million of spending for infrastructure improvements without bonding, Davis said.
A proposed three-year moratorium on new gaming licenses in the state failed to pass the state senate as amended and has died, Davis said.
The budget has been forwarded to Gov. Terry Branstad, who now has 30 business days to consider it. He has line-item veto powers.
Branstad said in a prepared statement released Tuesday night that he was "pleased" that legislators passed a budget that held spending to his recommended levels.
The state budget office has projected an $823 million generally accepted accounting principles surplus for fiscal 1997.
